title: Edge S2 Desktop: where to begin

segments.label: Opening: trading as a learned skill (Dr. Long, the Owl Group); the desktop takes the arithmetic off your hands: the risk box, the ladders, the bracket, split / merge / stop and reverse, one-click stop moves, the indicators on your time frames, Zero State
segments.title: Where to begin: a learned skill
segments.vo_script: Edge S2 Desktop is built on one idea from Dr. Long and the Owl Group: trading is a learned skill, and a skill can be mastered. The desktop takes the arithmetic off your hands. It works out the risk box for the symbol you are on. It draws the ladders from that box, up and down from the open. Every order is a bracket, with the stop one R against you and the target two R with you. It manages the trade: split a leg, merge legs, stop and reverse. One click moves the stop a quarter R, to no lose, or a quarter R past it. It watches the method's indicators on the time frames you trade, from one minute to daily, for the day trade and the swing, and names a setup at its bar. And when the tape has you, Zero State takes you away from it for a few minutes: the Owl, three breaths, gratitude, forgiveness, intention. With the tedious work gone, what is left is what Dr. Long teaches: the principles of trading mastery.

segments.label: Three colours: practice in green, paper in red, live in blue; the desktop does not change
segments.title: Three colours: practice, paper, live
segments.vo_script: One desktop. One way to place an order. Where the order goes is a colour. Green is practice. The desktop replays a day that already happened, and your order fills against that day's bars. No account is touched. Red is paper. The same order goes to your Interactive Brokers paper account, on today's market, with no money behind it. Blue is live. The same order goes to your live account. Nothing else changes: the same chart, the same ticket, the same keys. Practice in green. Test in red. Execute in blue. The hands learn one motion.
segments.anim_brief: a stylised S2 window whose frame takes the book colour; the same order pill leaves the same ticket for the practice book (a replayed day), the IB paper account, the IB live account; close on the three colours around one unchanged window

segments.label: Order types: the right-click menu reads the click against the mark; limit, short limit, stop-limit, market; the bracket at 1R and 2R; the stop never loosens
segments.title: Placing an order: the menu and the bracket
segments.vo_script: An order starts with a right-click on the chart. The menu reads where you clicked: the price at that level, and how far it sits from the mark. What it offers depends on which side you are on. Below the mark, a long limit: buy when price comes down to your level. Above the mark, a short limit: sell when price rises to it. A stop-limit enters the other way. A long stop-limit above the mark buys once price trades up through it. A short stop-limit below the mark sells on the way down. Market takes whatever prints. Every entry is a bracket. The stop sits one risk box against you. The target sits two risk boxes with you. Drag the target anywhere. The stop moves a quarter R at a time, and once it is placed it tightens or holds. It never loosens.

segments.label: Resting orders on the resting row; the fill; the position on the strip and its leg on the chart; the Stop panel; NL and NLQR
segments.title: Resting orders, the fill, the Stop panel
segments.vo_script: A placed bracket rests at IB. Its chip sits on the resting row above the chart: the stop, the target, the shares, and the dollars at risk. When the entry fills, the position appears on the book strip, and its leg draws on the chart: the entry, the risk, the open profit in R. The Stop panel on the right reads that leg. The stop moves a quarter R at a time, and two moves have names. NL puts the stop at your fill. No lose. NLQR puts it a quarter R past the fill. No lose, plus a quarter R: Dr. Long's dinner for two. A move is staged, then applied, and IB acknowledges it before the line moves.

segments.label: Legs: split a bracket into slices, merge legs into one bracket, stop and reverse; the new orders rest at IB before the old pair is cancelled
segments.title: Legs: split, merge, stop and reverse
segments.vo_script: A position is read as legs. One leg per bracket, with its own entry, its own risk, its own stop and target. E1, then E2 when you add. Split takes one leg and makes slices: a half, a third, or two thirds. Each slice gets its own stop and target, placed and acknowledged at IB before the old pair is cancelled. E1 becomes E1 a and E1 b. Merge works the other way. Tick the legs on the sheet, and every leg ticked becomes one bracket: one stop and one target for the shares together, at the blended entry, with the risks summed. Stop and reverse is one order from the right-click menu, on the losing side, like a stop. It is a stop for twice the position. Its fill closes the long and opens a short of the same size, with a stop one R past it and a target two R, good till cancelled. New orders rest at IB before the old ones leave, so the position is never uncovered.

segments.label: Risk management: the Risk box on the trade bar picks the basis, R10, R5, Frog or ATR14; the dollars a trade set what one R costs
segments.title: The Risk box: what one R is
segments.vo_script: Every stop and target is measured in R, and one R is a risk box. The Risk box on the trade bar picks the basis: R10, R5, Frog, or ATR14. Each one shows its size in price for the symbol you are on. Beside it, the dollars a trade: one hundred, four hundred, or a number you type. Pick a basis, set the dollars, and the shares follow: the dollars divided by one R. Every new bracket reads that box: one R of stop, two R of target. Change the basis, and the next bracket changes with it. Nothing to compute by hand.

segments.label: Draw risk boxes: long, top-left at the click and one R down; short, lower-left at the click and one R up; move, clip, delete
segments.title: Draw risk boxes
segments.vo_script: A risk box can also be drawn by hand. Right-click on the chart and the Draw group offers two. Place long risk box: its top-left corner at that price and bar, one R down from there, in green. Place short risk box: its lower-left corner at the click, one R up from there, in red. The box grows forward with the bars. Click a box to move it. Right-click it to clip it where it ends, or to delete it. One R on the chart, where you want to see it.

segments.label: Trade results: every closed trade recorded in $ and R; the Trades panel (Today: rows, the running curve in $ or R, the Histogram of R; History: NAV against its peak, a row per day); the trades on the chart as candles from the trade bar's On chart, each labelled with its R and Trade Pct
segments.title: Trade results: the list, the curve, the histogram, trades as candles
segments.vo_script: Every trade is recorded as it closes, in dollars and in R. Open the Trades panel and today's brackets are a list: one row per bracket, the entry and the exit, the risk it was placed with, the dollars, and the R. Below the rows, the R curve: a step per closed trade, as a running total or the last ten. Switch the view to Histogram and the day's trades fall into bins of R: half an R wide from minus two to plus one, one R beyond. History shows every day: the account against its peak, and a row per day in dollars and R. And the trades can sit on the chart. On the trade bar, beside the Stop panel, set On chart to Candles. Each closed trade is drawn as a candle on the bars it spanned: the body from the entry to the exit, the wicks the best and the worst price along the way, green or red by the result. And its label: the R, and the percent of the best price the exit kept.
